title: Convolution fools low-degree functions
statement: Let $\phi$ be a probability density on $\mathbb F_2^n$ whose nonzero Fourier coefficients all have absolute value at most $\varepsilon$, where $0<\varepsilon\leq1$. If $d\geq1$, then the $d$-fold convolution power of $\phi$ approximates the uniform expectation of every real sign encoding of an $\mathbb F_2$-valued function on $\mathbb F_2^n$ of algebraic degree at most $d$: the absolute difference between its expectation under that density and its uniform expectation is at most $9\varepsilon^{1/2^{d-1}}$.
hypotheses_covered: $\phi$ is a probability density on $\mathbb F_2^n$
Every nonzero Fourier coefficient of $\phi$ has absolute value at most $\varepsilon$
$d$ is a natural number with $1\leq d$
